topic: acoustic attributes in audio embeddings, spectral-metric contracts, and multi-objective spatial optimization

source_cards.title: Probing Low-Level Acoustic Attribute Encoding in CLAP Audio Embeddings
findings: RT60 and LUFS were approximately linearly decodable from several frozen embeddings under the study protocol
spectral centroid required nonlinear probes for complex music in most tested encoders
limitations: balanced synthetic perturbations differ from natural mix variation
music was downmixed to mono and segmented into 10-second chunks
spectral centroid was averaged over frames and is not a full spectral-balance descriptor
stereo, dynamics and musical preference were not evaluated
pitch shifting was used to expand spectral-centroid variation on real datasets

source_cards.title: SPHERE: Automatic Music Upmixing via Audio Language Model Post-Training with Spatial Heuristic Rewards
findings: six coupled rewards cover centering, spread and role-level balance
removing reward pairs produced reward hacking or spatial collapse
44 screened listeners preferred high-reward teacher binaural mixes in 338 of 440 trials
expert rating improvement from SFT to SFT+RL was small despite a larger objective-reward increase
limitations: binaural headphone upmix rather than conventional loudspeaker stereo
proprietary HRTF prevents exact rendering reproduction
23.5 percent of data excluded by context limit
expensive H100 training was used by the authors but not reproduced here

source_cards.title: TorchAudio SpectralCentroid implementation contract
verified: frequency bins are weighted by magnitude
output is a per-channel time series
sample rate, FFT size, window, hop, padding and window function are part of the metric contract
defaults differ from the DAFx paper configuration

knowledge_cards.claim: Feature decodability from an embedding does not make the embedding a calibrated acoustic meter.
Encoder preprocessing can destroy loudness information; model version and amplitude normalization are mandatory provenance.
A global spectral centroid does not describe spectral balance, masking, resonances or section roles.
Spectral metrics require an explicit FFT, window, hop, channel, activity and temporal-aggregation contract.
Semantic reference embeddings should be tested as auxiliary features while exact loudness and per-band anchors remain explicit.
Spatial optimization must jointly constrain center, spread and role-level balance to reduce collapse and reward hacking.
SPHERE reward-human alignment is evidence for selected binaural comparisons, not a universal stereo pan or width target.
Spotlight is a section role and may be vocal, lead guitar, riff or another element; vocal priority is not automatic.
Objective reward improvements may outpace preference improvements, so perceptual validation remains independent.

rule_candidates.when: an embedding is used to infer loudness, reverberation or spectral content
rule_candidates.change: retain a direct calibrated measurement and record model and preprocessing provenance
rule_candidates.test: compare against BS.1770 or the explicit target metric on song-disjoint data
rule_candidates.cancel: domain drift, bias or weaker-than-trivial baseline

rule_candidates.when: selecting an encoder for dynamics or level analysis
rule_candidates.change: test amplitude normalization and invariance before training or using a probe

rule_candidates.when: spectral centroid is computed for a stem or mix
rule_candidates.change: record FFT, window, hop, channel reduction, activity mask and aggregation; analyze by section
rule_candidates.test: compare multiple contracts and a per-band spectrum
rule_candidates.cancel: decision changes materially with windowing or silence proportion

rule_candidates.when: semantic reference matching proposes an EQ move
rule_candidates.change: test no-processing and level-only before a bounded EQ candidate
rule_candidates.test: loudness-matched blind full-mix A/B plus explicit per-band analysis
rule_candidates.cancel: embedding distance improves while musical preference or role clarity worsens

rule_candidates.when: optimizing pan, width or binaural position
rule_candidates.change: jointly evaluate center, spread and role-level balance
rule_candidates.test: ablate each objective and inspect collapse or extremes
rule_candidates.cancel: reward hacking, all-center collapse or exaggerated edges

rule_candidates.change: assign by section and permit non-vocal leads
rule_candidates.test: blind section comparison in the full mix
rule_candidates.cancel: fixed role conflicts with the intended focus

rule_candidates.when: adapting a SPHERE-like reward to the project
rule_candidates.change: validate binaural and loudspeaker stereo separately and derive local thresholds
rule_candidates.cancel: no direct evidence in the target playback condition
